open_obligations: Check that condition (1) holds for Du et al.'s fully connected ChatGPT copies.
Note that the martingale result concerns expected belief, not the probability of converging on a wrong answer.

out.other_title: Debates can converge confidently on an incorrect answer
out.rationale: Du et al. report debates can converge confidently on an incorrect answer. Choi, Zhu and Li prove that under Bayesian count updates and their condition (1) an agent's belief in the correct answer is a martingale, so debate alone does not raise expected correctness, which predicts consensus need not move toward truth; the model idealises agents as DCM samplers.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: why multi-agent debate can converge on incorrect answers, in a Dirichlet-multinomial model of homogeneous LLM agents

open_obligations: Note that a martingale allows individual wrong-to-right cases, so the conflict is about averages.
Check that Du et al.'s agents satisfy condition (1).
Check the empirically flat accuracy trajectories Choi et al. report on Du-like tasks.
out.other_title: Debate can reach a correct answer when all agents start wrong
out.rationale: Du et al. conclude from qualitative cases where all agents start wrong but end right that debate does not only amplify an initially present correct answer. Choi, Zhu and Li prove that under their Dirichlet-multinomial model with Bayesian count updates and condition (1), belief in the correct answer is a martingale, so debate alone does not raise expected correctness; individual cases can still go wrong-to-right under a martingale.
out.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: whether multi-agent debate itself improves correctness beyond amplifying initial answers

text: The authors prove that for any agent i at round t > 0, if the average previous-round belief in the correct answer over its neighbours equals the agent's own previous belief (condition (1)), then the agent's belief in the correct answer forms a martingale: its expected value at the next round equals its current value.
title: Multi-agent debate as a martingale: expected belief in the correct answer is unchanged
